note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
Obadiah is “concerning Edom”: the whole chapter is about Edom and what they did. “In the day that the strangers carried away captive his forces, and foreigners entered into his gates, and cast lots upon Jerusalem, even thou wast as one of them.” Even Edom was as one of them. First Esdras names the deed plainly: “Thou also hast vowed to build up the temple, which the Edomites burned when Judea was made desolate by the Chaldees.”

So who burned the temple? The Edomites. The history agrees: when the first temple was destroyed in 586 BC, Edom aided the Babylonian Empire rather than helping Judah, their brother. They rejoiced, looted the city, blocked the survivors fleeing, and took part in razing Solomon's temple. The brother of the Israelites assisted the Babylonians, which were Cushites, in destroying the first temple.

That is every charge in Obadiah. “Thou shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother in the day that he became a stranger”: the twelve tribes did become strangers. “Neither shouldest thou have rejoiced over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction”: they rejoiced when we got destroyed. They “laid hands on their substance”: they were robbing us too. They “stood in the crossway, to cut off those of his that did escape”: when we were escaping, Edom blocked our way, held us in, and gave us up to the Babylonians.

That is why the Psalm cries, “Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof.” Rase it: destroy it. That is what Edom did when they burned down that temple, and it is why Edom is called the daughter of Babylon, because they assisted the Cushite Babylonians: “O daughter of Babylon, who art to be destroyed”.

And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it. If thou therefore wilt worship me, all shall be thine.”

This Edomite is prideful because he has the spiritual power of Satan rolling with him. That is who gave him the power to go to the moon and to make these weapons to destroy all of mankind. No brown nation on the earth came up with the invention to destroy everybody; that belongs solely to the white man, because Satan is behind him. That is who he made a covenant with, not the God of the Bible.

So when you see In God we trust on the money, know he is not talking about anybody in this Bible. The Psalm proves it: “The wicked, through the pride of his countenance, will not seek after God: God is not in all his thoughts.” “The wicked in his pride doth persecute the poor”, and you judge whether a man is prideful or humble by how he treats the lowly: the blacks, Hispanics and Native Indians, who have no army. Out of all the kingdoms, Assyrian, Babylonian, Persian, Greek, Roman, none has been more prideful than Esau.

But the kingdoms Satan gives are not the Lord's, and Obadiah answers the pride: “thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord.” From the moment they said the Eagle has landed, they have been going down, because that is when the Israelites started hitting the streets with the word of God. The more we are gathered together, the more Esau comes down.

precepts.text: Evil shall hunt the violent man to overthrow him.
precepts.point: The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, saying, who shall bring me down to the ground? Trump now talks exactly like that.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
“The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” There is a set time for the times of the Gentiles to be fulfilled, with Esau at the top, that same spirit of Cain in rulership. But it is temporary. Waiting generation after generation for his judgment, the pride of his heart has deceived him. He forgot what his judgment is and thinks he is untouchable, especially after seeing what his weapons did to the air defences of Russia and China.

Now Trump is talking like that. On Air Force One after capturing Maduro he names the countries he will come after: Colombia, run by a sick man; Mexico, where the cartels are running things. He says the vice president of Venezuela will face a situation probably worse than Maduro, and emphasises how fast and violent it was: it was very violent. That office once had prestige, and though they did their evil, they at least spoke well. He is not even bothering with appearances anymore.

David shows where that ends: “Let not an evil speaker be established in the earth: evil shall hunt the violent man to overthrow him.” You reap what you sow. What he puts out is the exact same way his demise is going to come.

That is the lineage of Cain: Tubal-cain was “an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron”, and where others saw tools his mind saw weapons. Murder led to industry, hatred to technology, and violence to institutional power. Esau was told, “by thy sword shalt thou live.” But who shall bring him down to the ground? It is prophesied: first all those he dealt with will turn against him, and then Christ and his elect will have the glory and the honour to take him down.

precepts.text: The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, that saith, Who shall bring me down?
precepts.point: Edom is made small among the heathen and greatly despised. The pride of his heart has deceived him into thinking he is the wisest and most civilized of the earth.

note.label: War of the Gods

precepts.why:
The vision of Obadiah is a prophecy concerning Edom, a time to come, and we must be occupied in prophecies. The Lord says, “Behold, I have made thee small among the heathen: thou art greatly despised.” Edom will be greatly despised. Then he shows why: “The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee”. They are so prideful that they themselves are deceived.

“Thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock”: they are the cavemen. So Karen has nerve telling you don't park there, you don't belong here, being black while in Starbucks. You was in a cave. Now their pride has deceived them into thinking they are the wise of the earth, the most civilized of the earth. No: they are the most demonic of the earth.

“Whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” They ask that question as though they are God. Ezekiel shows the same prince of Tyrus, for Edom was also called Tyrus: “thou hast said, I am a God, I sit in the seat of God, in the midst of the seas; yet thou art a man, and not God”. Their bases sit in the midst of the seas. “Behold, thou art wiser than Daniel; there is no secret that they can hide from thee”: through all their technological advances they listen through your smart TV and your phone, and by that wisdom and traffic they got riches and lifted up their heart.

That pride grows from the weaponry given to that line from Tubal-cain and Lamech down to Esau, who by his sword would live. The Lord created the smith and the waster. In Isaiah the same one is called Lucifer and the king of Babylon, who weakened the nations through war: “I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the most High.” With all this military might they feel like they are the Most High, and people see it and say he must be God or God must be with them.

But the answer to “Who shall bring me down to the ground?” is the Lord. “How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer”. He is going to fall because his pride has reached up unto heaven, and when these devils fall, the whole earth will finally be at rest.

precepts.text: The cities of the tribe of Judah toward the south.
precepts.point: Carmel was Judah's and Bashan was Manasseh's.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
Before Obadiah, the class read Jeremiah 50:19: “And I will bring Israel again to his habitation, and he shall feed on Carmel and Bashan, and his soul shall be satisfied upon mount Ephraim and Gilead.” To know whose land Carmel and Bashan were, go back to the first dividing of the land in Joshua. Write it down: Carmel was Judah's.

Joshua 15 gives the cities of Judah: “And the uttermost cities of the tribe of the children of Judah toward the coast of Edom southward were Kabzeel, and Eder, and Jagur,” “And Kinah, and Dimonah”. Then jump to verse 55: “Maon, Carmel, and Ziph”. Those belonged to Judah. Judah's lot ran to the south, right up against the coast of Edom.

Jeremiah 50 goes on to say what God will do when he brings us back: “the iniquity of Israel shall be sought for, and there shall be none; and the sins of Judah, and they shall not be found: for I will pardon them whom I reserve.” He wipes away our iniquity and brings us again to our own habitation.

Then watch how things get switched around. Obadiah says “they of the south shall possess the mount of Esau.” The mount of Esau is where Edom used to dwell originally, and we are going to take that whole area. “and they of the plain the Philistines”: we are going to take Palestine. We shall possess the fields of Ephraim and the fields of Samaria. The land is ours by inheritance from the first dividing, and when God brings Israel back it will be possessed even further than it was then.

precepts.text: The inheritance of the half tribe of Manasseh, all Bashan.
precepts.point: Carmel was Judah's and Bashan was Manasseh's.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
Jeremiah 50:19 says Israel “shall feed on Carmel and Bashan”. Carmel was Judah's; now Bashan. Joshua 13 shows it: “And Moses gave inheritance unto the half tribe of Manasseh: and this was the possession of the half tribe of the children of Manasseh by their families.” “And their coast was from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the towns of Jair”. Bashan belonged to Manasseh.

Read Jeremiah 50:19 again so you get the thought: “And I will bring Israel again to his habitation, and he shall feed on Carmel and Bashan, and his soul shall be satisfied upon mount Ephraim and Gilead.” God is bringing Israel back to the very lands the tribes were given at the beginning.

Now see how it gets switched around in Obadiah. “And they of the south shall possess the mount of Esau; and they of the plain the Philistines: and they shall possess the fields of Ephraim, and the fields of Samaria: and Benjamin shall possess Gilead.” Benjamin shall possess Gilead. The tribes come back to the land, but the land is shared out anew.

Verse 20 goes on: “the captivity of this host of the children of Israel shall possess that of the Canaanites, even unto Zarephath”. The land of the Canaanites is the land of Israel, and Zarephath is Lebanon. “and the captivity of Jerusalem, which is in Sepharad, shall possess the cities of the south.” Sepharad is the Asia Minor region and Spain. Our people scattered there come home and take the cities of the south.

precepts.text: I will bring them into the land of Gilead and Lebanon, and place shall not be found for them.
precepts.point: Carmel was Judah's and Bashan was Manasseh's.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
Obadiah said “Benjamin shall possess Gilead”, and Zechariah shows God bringing us there: “I will bring them again also out of the land of Egypt, and gather them out of Assyria; and I will bring them into the land of Gilead”. He is going to take us out of captivity and bring us into the land of Gilead. That is Obadiah 19 that was just read.

Then “and Lebanon”. Who belongs in Lebanon? Go back to Obadiah verse 20: “the captivity of this host of the children of Israel shall possess that of the Canaanites, even unto Zarephath”, and Zarephath is Lebanon. “and the captivity of Jerusalem, which is in Sepharad, shall possess the cities of the south.” Then verse 21: “And saviours shall come up on mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau”, the mount of Edom.

Then “and place shall not be found for them.” There is not going to be enough room for us. Isaiah 49 says the same: “For thy waste and thy desolate places, and the land of thy destruction, shall even now be too narrow by reason of the inhabitants”. There will be too many of us. “and they that swallowed thee up shall be far away”: the nations that swallowed us up shall be far away.

Then: “The children which thou shalt have, after thou hast lost the other, shall say again in thine ears, The place is too strait for me: give place to me that I may dwell.” This place is too narrow; make room for me. That is why Christ said that in his Father's house are many mansions. Israel will come back in such numbers that the land cannot hold us.

precepts.text: Two parts shall be cut off and die, but the third shall be left.
precepts.point: Carmel was Judah's and Bashan was Manasseh's.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
Isaiah 49:20 speaks of “The children which thou shalt have, after thou hast lost the other”. The ones we lost are the two thirds, here in America. In case somebody asks what that means, Zechariah shows it: “And it shall come to pass, that in all the land, saith the Lord, two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein.”

Notice it says in all the land. The land it is talking about is Babylon, and that is America. So two out of every three Israelites shall die here in America. The ones we lost are them wicked Israelites.

Then the third: “And I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried: they shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people: and they shall say, The Lord is my God.”

That remnant is who goes back to possess the land in Obadiah. And even after the two thirds are gone, the children that are left shall say, “The place is too strait for me: give place to me that I may dwell.” The land will still be too narrow for the ones God brings back.

precepts.text: Though thou set thy nest among the stars, thence will I bring thee down.
precepts.point: They shall build, but God will throw down.

note.label: Christmas/ Icons, Idolatry, White Supremacy !!revealed!!

precepts.why:
Obadiah is spoken “concerning Edom”, the same Esau that God hated in Malachi. “Behold, I have made thee small among the heathen: thou art greatly despised.” God made him low, and he hated it.

“The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” That is the one who dwelt in the cliffs of the rocks, in the mountains: cave dwellers, Caucasians, troglodytes. He was displaced out of his land and ended up in the Caucasus Mountains, and when he gained power on the earth he said in his heart that nobody could bring him down.

“Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle”: Greece, Rome, Spain, Portugal, they all rose up as the eagle, and America rose up as the eagle. “And though thou set thy nest among the stars”: gaining power out in space, space travel. How did he get to the stars? Because Satan gave him power to do it: technology, rockets, rocket science, nuclear bombs.

“Thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord.” It is the same thing God said in Malachi. Edom said “we will return and build the desolate places”: the Renaissance, the rebirth, building up Europe into a superpower on the earth. “They shall build, but I will throw down”. They will rise up again in power, but the Most High himself will bring them down, and they are “the border of wickedness”, the beginning and the end of all wickedness on the earth, with his people, “against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.”

precepts.point: So the question is whether that same mercy extends to Edom, and the scriptures answer it.

precepts.point: Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir. Mount Seir is the clefts of the rock; the vision of Obadiah speaks to Edom as thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose pride hath deceived him.

note.label: Genesis 36: The Generations of Esau, Who Is Edom

Mount Seir is the clefts of the rock. “Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.” He went from the face of his brother rich out of the house of Isaac and Abraham, their riches more than that they might dwell together, as with Abram and Lot in Genesis 13; and where he settled is the high habitation whose pride hath deceived him.

precepts.text: The wise men of Edom and the mighty men of Teman shall be destroyed, that every one of the mount of Esau may be cut off.

note.label: Genesis 36: The Generations of Esau, Who Is Edom

precepts.why:
“Shall I not in that day, saith the Lord, even destroy the wise men out of Edom, and understanding out of the mount of Esau? And thy mighty men, O Teman, shall be dismayed, to the end that every one of the mount of Esau may be cut off by slaughter.”

Much of the world's science and weapons technology has come out of Germany, and the word says that wisdom will be destroyed: the wise men out of Edom, understanding out of the mount of Esau, and the mighty men of Teman dismayed, to the end that every one of the mount of Esau may be cut off.

precepts.text: The house of Jacob shall be a fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble; there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau.
precepts.point: Out of Jacob shall come he that shall have dominion: that is the one who cometh from Edom with dyed garments from Bozrah, glorious in his apparel, traveling in the greatness of his strength, which is the whole host of heaven, thousands upon thousands of angels. The day of vengeance is in his heart, for though Israel serves out her punishment in captivity, Esau went overboard and kept laying on punishment when our iniquity had an end.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
Edom shall be a possession, but for Esau that servitude is not for ever, because Esau is the only nation on the earth with an expiration date.

“And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble, and they shall kindle in them, and devour them; and there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau; for the Lord hath spoken it.” The house of Jacob, the twelve tribes of Israel, the blacks, Hispanics, and Native Indians, shall be a fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble.

There shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau, for the Lord hath spoken it. The rest of the nations go into servitude for ever, but the Lord can only bear with Esau so much longer; that is Israel doing valiantly.

precepts.text: Thou shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother in the day that he became a stranger; the brother becoming a stranger is the key to who Moses means.
precepts.point: The stranger of this commandment is thy brother fallen into decay, whom thou shalt relieve, not the nations Israel was commanded to drive out.

note.label: Deuteronomy 10: What Doth the Lord Require of Thee

precepts.why:
Which stranger is Moses telling Israel to love? Obadiah gives the key: “But thou shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother in the day that he became a stranger; neither shouldest thou have rejoiced over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction”. The brother became a stranger. Moses is prophesying of the day Israel's own brother would become a stranger: when the northern kingdom was cut off, the brother became the stranger who would come back.

“Love ye therefore the stranger: for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt.” The stranger the Lord loves, “in giving him food and raiment”, is that brother who became a stranger. Love them, because they are coming back into the covenant. The commandment is not about the nations Israel was commanded to drive out; it is about thy brother.

precepts.text: The day that he became a stranger: Israel became strangers when they were displaced out of their homeland.
precepts.point: Israel became strangers in the day they were displaced out of their homeland, as Obadiah says of the day of Jacob's captivity. The peculiar people given the peculiar laws of God is Israel, and that is what is taught to our people today, raising them back up into the understanding of who they are and that we must repent in order to get the kingdom.

note.label: Deuteronomy 14: A Peculiar People and the Clean Foods

precepts.why:
How did the peculiar people become strangers? Obadiah speaks of “the day of thy brother in the day that he became a stranger”, “the children of Judah in the day of their destruction”, “the day of distress”. Israel became strangers in the day they were displaced out of their homeland, the day of Jacob's captivity.

That is why Peter writes to strangers scattered: the peculiar people chosen above all the nations were scattered out of their land and made strangers in it.

The peculiar people given the peculiar laws of God is Israel, and that is what is taught to our people today, raising them back up into the understanding of who they are and that we must repent in order to get the kingdom.

precepts.text: The house of Jacob is a fire and Esau is stubble; none of the house of Esau shall remain, for the Lord has spoken it.
precepts.point: The only way the wickedness of the wicked comes to an end is that they die. The wicked is the so-called white man according to the bible, and his end is inevitable. This is God's word, not man's; do not try to get God's enemy out of the way.

note.label: Psalm 7: David's Prayer for Deliverance in the Last Days

precepts.why:
The wicked in Psalm 7:9 is the so-called white man according to the bible, and his end is inevitable. Obadiah spells it out: “And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble, and they shall kindle in them, and devour them; and there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau; for the Lord hath spoken it.”

The house of Jacob is a fire and Esau is stubble. None of the house of Esau shall remain. That is how the wickedness of the wicked comes to an end, and how the just are established.

This is God's word, not man's: “for the Lord hath spoken it.” Do not try to get God's enemy out of the way yourself. The Most High has already declared the end of Esau.

precepts.text: Esau's pride and desire to exalt himself as God brings the Most High's promise to bring him down.
precepts.point: Esau does not regard the operations of the Most High; they want to be as God, above God, in their sciences and everything their hands touch. But the wicked, whether Esau or our own people, will not be built back up once destroyed. When those bombs hit, they are gone.

note.label: Psalm 28: Be Not Silent To Me

precepts.why:
“Because they regard not the works of the Lord, nor the operation of his hands, he shall destroy them, and not build them up.” That is Esau. Esau does not regard the operations of the Most High; they want to be as God, above God, in their sciences and everything their hands touch.

“The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground? Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars, thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord.” Esau's pride and desire to exalt himself as God brings the Most High's promise to bring him down.

And the wicked, whether Esau or our own people, will not be built back up once destroyed. When those bombs hit, they are gone. He gives them according to their deeds, and destroys them, and does not build them up.

precepts.text: The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock; this is a proud man.
precepts.point: The man of sin has to be revealed, and our people still do not want to acknowledge that Esau is the devil, not Christ. The white picture of Jesus is a deception; the Bible says nothing like that.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

Obadiah speaks to Edom: “The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” This is a proud man, the boasting mighty man of Psalm 52.

The man of sin has to be revealed, and our people still do not want to acknowledge that Esau is the devil, not Christ. The white picture of Jesus is a deception; the Bible says nothing like that. The pride of Esau's heart has deceived him, and he thinks no one will bring him down.

precepts.text: Esau is condemned for entering the gate of the Most High's people in their calamity and laying hands on their substance.

In this captivity Esau still profits off our labour and our inventions, the light filament, the plasma and open heart surgery, the cotton gin, computers and cell phones, yet makes no account of who produced them.

note.label: Proverbs 5: The Strange Woman and Thy Labours in the House of a Stranger

Obadiah names the stranger who did it: Esau. “But thou shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother in the day that he became a stranger; neither shouldest thou have rejoiced over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction; neither shouldest thou have spoken proudly in the day of distress. Thou shouldest not have entered into the gate of my people in the day of their calamity; yea, thou shouldest not have looked on their affliction in the day of their calamity, nor have laid hands on their substance in the day of their calamity”.

Esau is condemned for entering the gate of the Most High's people in their calamity and laying hands on their substance. That substance is our labours in the house of a stranger.

We are living this now. In this captivity Esau still profits off our labour and our inventions, the light filament, the plasma and open heart surgery, the cotton gin, computers and cell phones, yet makes no account of who produced them. He laid hands on our substance in the day of our calamity, just as Obadiah says.

note.label: Ezekiel 25: Judgment on Ammon, Moab, Edom, and the Philistines
